drugs in a white VW Gol. The driver tried to flee when the patrol car
approached, was chased for a few blocks and caught. The driver, a
30-year-old man, was taken to the Água Clara police station.

weighing about 54 kilograms. Two men were arrested at that address.

and stopped with about 500 grams of marijuana and a precision scale.

police said the first suspect had discarded during the roadside approach.

phones, packaging material and about 250 reais in cash.

charged with drug dealing and association with drug dealing, and the fifth was
captured under an open arrest warrant. The tablets were hidden in a wooded
area near the MS-324 highway. The operation ran from the night of Wednesday
4 November into the morning of Thursday 5 November.

October 2026 during an operation at an industrial warehouse in Cabanes, Girona. The operation seized 8,025 kg of hashish at the warehouse.

truck, apparently preparing to load the hashish into vans for distribution.
Inspection showed the hashish was hidden among other goods inside large raffia
sacks filled with rubber chippings, a method used to defeat police and customs

The investigation began in June 2026 after police intercepted a van in
Viladecans, Barcelona, and linked its cargo to the Cabanes warehouse. EFE
reported that the police investigation began in July, after officers located a
van in Viladecans, Barcelona. The seven men were placed before the Civil
and Instruction Section of the Court of First Instance in Figueres, and the
investigation remains open.

Police valued the seized hashish at more than 16.2 million euros on the illicit
market. Europa Press, citing a Mossos d'Esquadra statement, reported that
seven men aged 29 to 55 were detained on 1 October over 8,025 kilos of hashish
stored in the Cabanes warehouse.

report.title: Ceuta port truck driver jailed after UDYCO seized about 300 kg hashish
report.summary: Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta after finding bags of hashish hidden in a false bottom, estimated at about 300 kilograms. On Sunday 15 November 2026 a judge ordered the driver held in preventive detention for an offence against public health; the investigation remains open.
report.body:
Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta carrying a
stash of hashish hidden in a sophisticated false bottom. The arrest took place on Friday 13 November 2026. Officers
intercepted the truck on the port road at the Muelle de Poniente and searched it
with support from the UPR prevention unit and the canine group. They found
the hashish and detained the driver, showing him the drugs found in the vehicle
he was driving.

The truck appeared empty and was heading toward boarding for Spain when a
specialist drugs dog alerted, prompting an exhaustive hours-long search inside
and outside the vehicle. After the hours-long detailed inspection, officers
found a large number of bags full of hashish inside the truck's structure.
Officers recovered numerous bags of hashish from the trailer's false bottom,
with first estimates putting the haul above 300 kilograms although police gave
no official weight. The bags of hashish were loaded into a police van for transport and the pending official weighing. Police had to break open the metal sheet hiding the false bottom with hammers, shears, sledgehammers and an angle grinder. The submitted account describes the seizure as about
300 kilograms of hashish arriving from Morocco.

The handcuffed driver was taken to police headquarters and placed under
investigation for an offence against public health. On Sunday 15 November 2026 the driver was brought before a judge, who ordered preventive detention for an offence against public health. Police link the
operation to open UDYCO investigations into groups moving hashish from Ceuta to
mainland Spain in heavy vehicles with hidden compartments. The investigation remains open, with police suspecting larger loads and the hiding of heavy vehicles in spaces used as stores for hashish.

report.body:
National Police officers arrested four men and a woman in Palma on suspicion of
belonging to a group dedicated to drug trafficking. Group I of the
Narcotics Division of the National Police said it had closed an investigation
begun months earlier that ended with five detainees.

Officers identified a man living in Palma as the recipient of a hashish parcel,
seized the package containing 24 kilos of hashish and arrested him for suspected
drug trafficking. In the first home, that of the main suspect, officers
found 36 kilos of hashish, an air rifle with silencer and about 10,000 euros in
cash. The man and a woman were then arrested as the alleged authors of drug
trafficking and membership of a criminal group or organisation.

In the second home the officers arrested a second suspect who allegedly kept and
transported the drugs, and found two kilos of cocaine, prepared doses, cutting
agent, a pistol with 9 mm cartridges and a bow with arrows. A fifth person
was arrested because of their connection to the case.

Officers of the Unidad de Prevención y Reacción, Group II of the Narcotics
Division and the canine unit also took part in the searches.

The Manacor Manacor account reports the same operation: a parcel with 24 kilos
of hashish intercepted and two home searches yielding 36 more kilos, for a total
of 60 kilos. Última Hora reports that 36 kilos of hashish, an air rifle
with silencer and about 10,000 euros in cash were found in the home of the main
suspect.

report.body:
Police Narcotics Bureau officers arrested three Thai nationals at Bandaranaike
International Airport in Katunayake early on 15 October 2026 as they attempted
to leave the airport with narcotics. The three suspects, aged 22, 22 and
33, are drivers by profession in Thailand. Officers of the Katunayake
Airport Police Narcotics Bureau arrested the suspects as they tried to leave the
airport. The suspects were arrested by officers of the Police Narcotics
Bureau on Thursday after arriving on a flight from Bangkok, Thailand.

The three suspects arrived at Katunayake Airport from Bangkok on Thai Airways
flight TG-307 at approximately 12.30 a.m. on 15 October 2026. During an
inspection of their three pieces of luggage, officers discovered 5.96 kilograms
of hashish concealed inside cosmetic product containers. A search of their
luggage uncovered 5 kilograms and 96 grams of hashish concealed inside cosmetic
cream containers in three travel bags. The contraband was concealed inside
containers meant for cosmetic products to evade standard customs screening.
Police valued the seizure at Rs. 51 million. Investigators said the
suspects had allegedly concealed the narcotics in cosmetic and beauty-care
products and attempted to smuggle them into Sri Lanka. According to
investigators, the suspects had allegedly attempted to smuggle the narcotics
into Sri Lanka by hiding the drug consignment inside cosmetic and beauty-care
items.

The suspects and the seized drugs were scheduled to be produced before the
Negombo Magistrate's Court on 15 October for further legal proceedings. The
Airport Police Narcotics Bureau was conducting further investigations. The
Police Narcotics Bureau continued its active investigation to uncover wider
trafficking links.

report.title: NDLEA Rivers State: 281 arrested and 54 convictions between July and October 2026
report.summary: NDLEA's Rivers State Command said it arrested 281 suspected drug offenders between July and October 2026 and secured 54 convictions, seizing 316.152 kg of illicit substances in a total that gives no separate weight for cannabis. State commander Offor Kenneth Onyeso warned that dealers recruit children aged 12 to 16 to move drugs.
report.body:
Between July and October 2026, Nigeria's National Drug Law Enforcement Agency
said its Rivers State Command arrested 281 suspected drug offenders, 238 men and
43 women. State commander Offor Kenneth Onyeso gave the figures at a press
briefing. The seizures that followed weighed 316.152 kg, made up of 288.695
kg of narcotic drugs and 27.457 kg of psychotropic substances. The command
filed 74 cases in court in the period and secured 54 convictions, with 276 cases
still pending.

The commander said drug dealers were recruiting children aged 12 to 16 to
distribute narcotics. He told parents and guardians that dealers were
exploiting minors to evade prosecution, knowing that children might not be
subjected to the same legal consequences as adult offenders.

He identified Abuja Dam in Port Harcourt and Obio/Akpor local government area as
major drug hotspots where the command carried out raids and made arrests and
seizures. Operations at Abuja Dam and Abonnema Wharf received support from
the Nigerian Navy, Army, Police and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps. He also listed Port Harcourt City and Obio/Akpor local government areas as
vulnerable areas for drug activity. He warned about the circulation of
high-grade cannabis, tramadol and methamphetamine, known locally as Mkpurumini,
in the state. The command said it would intensify operations against
identified drug hotspots ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Beyond enforcement, the command said 17 people were admitted to its
rehabilitation facility during the period, 143 received brief intervention
services and 277 underwent drug integrity tests. It ran 48 enlightenment
and advocacy programmes in schools, communities, workplaces, markets,
non-governmental organisations and religious institutions, reaching 150,942
people.

report.body:
Two men were arrested on 13 November 2026 by the research brigade of the
Yeumbeul Sud police station in an operation against a suspected kush-trafficking
network in Thiaroye Kao, in the Dakar suburbs. The operation followed an
anonymous tip about heavy kush trafficking, and plainclothes investigators
raided the reported location at around 8 a.m.

The first suspect, P. Ngom, was caught near the Thiaroye market apparently
packaging narcotics, and a search of the spot found 20 pieces of kush cannabis
hidden in a disused vehicle tyre. On him police also found 3,000 CFA francs
and an Infinix mobile phone. The second suspect, E. L. Welle, was arrested
near the footbridge of the Thiaroye TER train station, where a pat-down found 24
pieces of kush concealed under his clothing.

Police seized 44 pieces of kush in total, along with 3,000 CFA francs and a
mobile phone, and sealed the material for the legal proceedings. Both
suspects said they owned the seized narcotics but refused to reveal their
supplier's identity. The public prosecutor was informed and an
investigation was opened to determine the extent of the suspects' activities and
to identify their supplier.

Thai immigration police and officers of the Department of Thai Traditional and
Alternative Medicine searched a three-storey rented house in Khubon 27 Road in
the Tha Raeng area of Bang Khen district, Bangkok, on 19 October 2026, under a
search warrant from the Min Buri Criminal Court. Officers arrested one
Vietnamese man and four workers from Myanmar, who were sorting and packing
cannabis buds for delivery to customers when police entered the house.
Police suspect the Vietnamese man was managing the daily operations, and the
four Myanmar workers earned 200 to 300 baht a day for their work.

Police seized more than five tonnes of cannabis buds, packed in black bags and
hidden throughout the house's three floors. Police said the house had a
ventilator outlet that discharged the cannabis smell into the surrounding space. Officers spent about two months gathering evidence after residents

and the foreign nationals had lived and run the business at the house for more
than a year.

province, which does not cover Bangkok, so the operation in Bangkok broke the
Thai Traditional Medicine Protection and Promotion Act, which carries up to one
year in prison or a fine of 20,000 baht. Police are sending the seized
cannabis to a laboratory to determine whether it was grown in Thailand or
imported. Investigators are tracing the Thai person who rented the
property, the source of the cannabis and any financiers behind the operation.

report.body:
The Ingulskyi district court of Mykolaiv sentenced a 51-year-old local man to
nine years in prison for growing cannabis on his garden plot and storing dried
and ground cannabis in his attic. The Mykolaiv city prosecutor's office
said the court found him guilty of illegal manufacture and storage of narcotics
for sale in particularly large quantities and of growing cannabis, under
articles 307(3) and 310(1) of the criminal code. The sentence came without
confiscation of property.

Officers of police department No 2 of the Mykolaiv district police department
uncovered the man's activity in July 2026 and searched his place of residence. The search yielded more than 10 kilograms of dried cannabis raw material
and 14 cannabis plants. Police searched the suspect's home on 25 July 2026. The prosecutor's office put the cannabis stored in the attic of the house
at more than 8 kilograms. Novosti N called the difference between the two
official figures a small discrepancy: more than 10 kilograms of dried cannabis
raw material in the police release against more than 8 kilograms of cannabis in
the prosecutor's statement.

The court established that the man had been growing cannabis on his property
since April 2026. He dried part of the harvest in his attic and ground the
rest into glass jars for storage and, according to investigators, for sale.
Investigators detained him in July under article 208 of the criminal procedure
code and notified him of suspicion. When the police announced the case in
July they said the offence carried up to 12 years in prison with confiscation of
property. During the pre-trial investigation the court put the suspect
under custody with the option of posting bail.

At the trial the suspect partly admitted his guilt, saying he grew the plants
only for his own use, and the court dismissed that account as an attempt to
avoid liability. The court noted that he had already served five years in
prison for growing cannabis. He was also charged 28,400 hryvnias for the
cost of the expert examinations, and the court ordered the seized plants and
cannabis destroyed. The verdict has not entered into force and may be
appealed to the Mykolaiv appeal court within 30 days of its pronouncement.

The accounts give no description of the property or of the size of the grow.
It is not stated whether the pesticides found at the site had been used on the plants.
Every account repeats the same Kern County Sheriff's Office statement, so no independent reporting of the search is available.
report.body:
Kern County sheriff's deputies from the Taft substation, assisted by the Kern
County Sheriff's Office High Intensity Drug Trafficking Areas Task Force
(KC-HIDTA) and the Taft Police Department, executed a search warrant in the
27000 block of Highway 119 in Taft on 8 October 2026. The warrant was
served at a property in Valley Acres. Rogelio Lorenzo Francisca, 32, from
Guerrero, Mexico, was arrested and booked into the Taft jail facility.
Deputies assigned to the Taft Substation, assisted by the task force and the
Taft Police Department, executed the same warrant in the 27000 block of Highway
119 on 8 October. Kern County Sheriff's Office officials reported that the
warrant was executed in the 27000 block of Highway 119 in Taft on 8 October. Francisca was charged with cultivating marijuana, marijuana for sale,
conspiracy and delaying, resisting or obstructing an arrest.

During the search deputies eradicated 660 marijuana plants. Authorities
located and eradicated a total of 660 marijuana plants during the search.
Investigators also found dangerous pesticides at the grow site. The
pesticides found at the cultivation site raised safety concerns.

The Kern County Sheriff's Office said the investigation is active and ongoing. Authorities have not released further details of the operation.

cases.title: South Africa legalises private cannabis use
cases.why: A change in the law (the Cannabis for Private Purposes Act, signed in May 2024). Law changes go to the Cannabis Freedom Index history, not into the tracker.

attempts.decision_title: Legalisation of cannabis for private use goes to the CFI history
attempts.explanation: The submitted article reports the signing of South Africa's Cannabis for Private Purposes Act, which removes cannabis from the list of outlawed narcotics and makes private cultivation and consumption by adults lawful, with trading and medicinal-only dispensary sales still outside the law. That is a change in the country's drug law and its score, which the editorial rules place in the Cannabis Freedom Index's country history rather than in this enforcement tracker, so no tracker report is created. The article also recounts the 2018 Constitutional Court ruling in the Prince case that made private cannabis consumption constitutional and the police order to end pot busts from 2023; the ruling is a precedent and the order is a policy change, so both also belong to the CFI history rather than to a report here. The only enforcement episode mentioned, the 2020 raid on the Haze Club in Johannesburg with proceedings continuing, is stated in one sentence without figures and does not appear among existing reports; it could be drafted as its own report if an account with quantities and dates is found.
